name: OProver
abstract: OProver is a unified framework for agentic formal theorem proving in Lean4: retrieval, compiler feedback, and multi-round repair are built into training itself rather than bolted on at inference. OProver-32B sets the open-weight state of the art on MiniF2F and outperforms a 671B prover across all five of its evaluations.
contributions: Unifies retrieval augmentation, Lean4 compiler feedback, and iterative repair with the training strategy and data construction, instead of treating them as inference-time modules.
Releases OProofs: 1.77M Lean statements with 6.86M compiler-verified proofs and serialized proving trajectories, including failed attempts and repairs.
OProver-32B reaches 93.3 on MiniF2F (Pass@32), state of the art among open-weight whole-proof provers, beating DeepSeek-Prover-V2 at 671B on all five reported benchmarks.
method: Continued pretraining is followed by iterative post-training: each round runs agentic proving, indexes newly verified proofs into the retrieval memory, converts repair trajectories to SFT data, and sends unresolved cases to RL.
At inference the prover retrieves compiler-verified proofs, attempts a proof, and revises against Lean4 compiler feedback across rounds.
Pass@32 rises monotonically through the loop: OProver-8B climbs from 79.5 to 91.8 on MiniF2F across three rounds.
